header.running_head: The Sahabah (RA) Endure Hardships and difficulties when Giving Da'wah towards Allaah

Abu Jahal bin Hishaam said, "Someone has mentioned that you have forsaken your religion?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) declared: "I testify that there is none worthy of worship but the One Allaah Who has no partner and that Muhammad ﷺ is Allaah's servant and Rasul."

When the Mushrikeen got up to assault him, Hadhrat Umar (RA) attacked Utba bin Rabee'ah and (after overpowering him) squatted over him and continued beating him up and poking his fingers in his eyes until Utba screamed. (Fearing that Hadhrat Umar (RA) would make their leader blind, the others retreated.) Hadhrat Umar (RA) stood up (and left Utba) once the others had moved away. In the same way, whenever any group approached him (to assault him), he would grab hold of their leader (would beat him up and threaten to blind him) until the others gave up. He then proceeded to all the gatherings he used to frequent (as a Kaafir) and proclaimed the message of Imaan there.

After asserting his dominance over the Mushrikeen, Hadhrat Umar (RA) went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "May my parents be sacrificed for you! By Allaah! You now have no fear. Without any fear or trepidation, I have proclaimed the message of Imaan in every gathering I used to frequent as a Kaafir." With Hadhrat Umar (RA) in front of him, Rasulullaah ﷺ went with Hadhrat Hamza (RA) to the Masjidul Haraam where they performed Tawaaf of the Kabah and then performed the Zuhr salaah without any fear. Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ returned to house of Hadhrat Arqam (RA) in the company of Hadhrat Umar (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) later left by himself and then Rasulullaah ﷺ also left.
The most correct opinion is that Hadhrat Umar (RA) accepted Islaam only after some Sahabah (RA) had migrated to Abyssinia, which was six years after Rasulullaah ﷺ announced his prophethood.[^1]
Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) leaves for Abyssinia when the Muslims Face Intense Harassment and Meets Ibnud Daghina

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I never knew my parents to be adherents of any religion besides the Deen of Islaam. Not a day passed when Rasulullaah ﷺ did not visit us every morning and night. When the Muslims were being harassed greatly, (my father) Abu Bakr decided to migrate to Abyssinia. When he reached a place called Barkul Ghimaad, Ibnud Daghina who was the leader of the Qaara tribe met him and asked, 'Where are you off to, O Abu Bakr?'
